_meta.description: Canonical daily verse for this Next.js app — bump version when today or catalog changes; keep KJV text exact. For static-site parity, mirror into root script.js ROTATING_HERO_VERSES / daily pickers when you change pilot day.

today.text: For the mountains shall depart, and the hills be removed; but my kindness shall not depart from thee, neither shall the covenant of my peace be removed, saith the LORD that hath mercy on thee.

breakdown.speaker: The Lord God, spoken through the prophet Isaiah
breakdown.audience: Jerusalem — God’s people who felt abandoned, afraid He’d walk away
breakdown.relatesToToday: In 2026 everything still feels shaky: jobs, health, headlines, your own mood. This verse says the stuff that looks permanent can move — but God’s kindness and His peace-deal with you don’t.
breakdown.relatesToYou: If you’re braced for the other shoe to drop, this is God locking eyes with you: I’m not leaving. Your peace isn’t a mood you have to manufacture; it’s tied to Him.
breakdown.realTalk: Mountains are the big, unmovable things in your head. God says even those can shift — and He still won’t budge on caring for you. That’s the whole point.

kid.relatesToToday: Sometimes big things feel scary or confusing. This verse says God’s love for you stays put even when stuff changes.
kid.relatesToYou: God is kind like someone who stays with you on a hard day — He doesn’t walk off because you had a meltdown or a bad grade.
kid.realTalk: When things shift, God’s kindness stays. He keeps His peace-promise for you.

teen.relatesToToday: When life feels unstable — family, friends, future — this verse says what’s true about God doesn’t depend on your circumstances staying perfect.
teen.relatesToYou: If you’re waiting for the next thing to go wrong, God says His care isn’t a temporary vibe. It’s covenant-level faithful.
teen.realTalk: The big stuff in life can shift. God’s commitment to you and His peace doesn’t. That’s what you can actually lean on.

adult.relatesToToday: When you’re running on fumes — night shift, grief, little kids, bills — the world keeps rearranging. This line grounds you: God’s kindness and the peace He gives aren’t tied to things holding still.
adult.relatesToYou: You don’t have to earn His steadiness. Mercy is in the sentence on purpose — He’s not waiting for you to get it together before He stays.
adult.realTalk: It’s plain: landscapes can change; God’s kindness toward you doesn’t. That’s bedrock when your Tuesday is a mess.

today.quietPrayerNudge: Lord, hold me in Your kindness today.
verseEchoPrompts: Lord, when everything feels unstable, hold me in Your kindness.
Thank You that Your peace isn’t something I have to muscle up.
Teach me to rest in the covenant You keep — not in my circumstances.

catalog.text: But they that wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not be faint.

breakdown.speaker: The Lord God, through the prophet Isaiah
breakdown.audience: A weary people — exiles who felt finished, and anyone whose strength has run out
breakdown.relatesToToday: We live wired for hurry: notifications, shifts that don’t end, kids who need you before you’ve had coffee. This verse names a different source of fuel — not grit alone, but waiting on God on purpose.
breakdown.relatesToYou: You’re not weak because you’re tired. God offers renewal when you stop pretending you can white-knuckle everything and actually look to Him for the next step.
breakdown.realTalk: Waiting here isn’t sitting and doing nothing. It’s leaning on God instead of your own panic. When you do, He trades your empty tank for strength that lasts the long day.

kid.relatesToToday: Sometimes you feel too tired to keep going. God says people who trust Him get new strength — like wings to keep moving.
kid.relatesToYou: When school or feelings wear you out, God helps you not give up — not because you’re perfect, but because you look to Him.
kid.realTalk: When you’re tired, God refills you. He gives strength for the next step.

teen.relatesToToday: Burnout isn’t just for adults. When you’re overloaded, this verse says strength comes from waiting on God — not from forcing everything yourself.
teen.relatesToYou: If you’re running on empty, God isn’t judging your limits. He invites you to rely on Him and catch your breath for real.
teen.realTalk: “Wait on the Lord” means hang your weight on Him instead of on your own nerves. That’s how strength comes back.

adult.relatesToToday: In 2026 the grind is real: caregiving, grief, night work, anxiety that won’t clock out. This verse doesn’t shame your weariness — it points you to God as the one who renews.
adult.relatesToYou: You don’t have to mount up like an eagle every morning on your own. One honest “I need You” counts as waiting on Him.
adult.realTalk: Plain and simple: stop, look to God, let Him strengthen you. Then you can walk the next hour without collapsing.

catalog.quietPrayerNudge: Lord, renew my strength for this one step.
verseEchoPrompts: Lord, renew my strength today — I wait on You.
Teach me what it means to wait on You, not rush my own fix.
Thank You for patience with me when I am weary.

catalog.text: Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.

breakdown.speaker: Paul, writing by the Spirit to believers
breakdown.audience: The church at Philippi — ordinary people learning joy under real pressure
breakdown.relatesToToday: Anxiety is the background noise of modern life — inboxes, health alerts, money, kids. Paul doesn’t say “pretend you’re fine.” He says bring it to God, with thanks mixed in, and let His peace stand guard.
breakdown.relatesToYou: Your mind doesn’t have to be a hostile place. Peace here is God’s own calm standing watch over what you cannot argue into silence.
breakdown.realTalk: Don’t spin alone. Tell God what you need, say thank you for what He’s already done, and His peace — the kind you can’t explain — starts guarding your head and heart.

kid.relatesToToday: When worries bounce in your head, God wants you to talk to Him and say thank you too — not fake happy, just honest.
kid.relatesToYou: You can tell God what scares you. He listens, and He helps your inside feel safer.
kid.realTalk: Tell God what’s wrong and say thanks too. He gives peace like a guard for your thoughts.

teen.relatesToToday: School, friends, family, future — it piles up. This verse says swap endless looping for prayer plus gratitude, and God’s peace takes post in your mind.
teen.relatesToYou: You don’t have to win the argument in your head before you come to God. Bring the mess; He meets you there.
teen.realTalk: Honest requests + thanks = room for God’s peace to stand guard. You’re not weak for needing that.

adult.relatesToToday: When your mind races at 2 AM or your chest tightens over bills, this is a kitchen-table practice: name the worry, hand it up, fold in thanks, and let God’s peace do security detail.
adult.relatesToYou: You’re not failing if you need help with your thoughts. This is God doing what you cannot — keeping you through Christ.
adult.realTalk: No performance. Just prayer, specifics, gratitude, and peace that outranks what you can figure out alone.

catalog.quietPrayerNudge: Lord, I bring my worry to You — thank You for hearing me.
verseEchoPrompts: Lord, I bring my worry to You — thank You for hearing me.
Thank You for peace that passes what I can figure out on my own.

catalog.text: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.

breakdown.speaker: Jesus Christ
breakdown.audience: Anyone who is tired — soul-tired, body-tired, tired of trying to hold it all
breakdown.relatesToToday: We wear busyness like a badge and wonder why we’re hollow. Jesus cuts through: come as you are, not after you’ve fixed the spreadsheet of your life.
breakdown.relatesToYou: Rest isn’t reward for being strong enough. It’s what He gives when you stop performing and actually come to Him.
breakdown.realTalk: If you’re carrying more than you can hold, Jesus says come. No prerequisites. He gives real rest — not collapse, not numbness, but His kind of relief.

kid.relatesToToday: When you feel worried or worn out, Jesus says come to Him and He helps you rest inside.
kid.relatesToYou: You don’t have to be big and brave first. Jesus wants you to come to Him exactly as you are.
kid.realTalk: Tired kids can come to Jesus. He gives rest — a deep breath for your heart.

teen.relatesToToday: Pressure to measure up is loud. Jesus invites you before you’ve got it all sorted — and He gives rest that isn’t fake chill.
teen.relatesToYou: You don’t have to earn a break from Him. Show up honest, and He meets you.
teen.realTalk: “Come” is the whole move. Heavy laden counts as qualified. He handles the rest part.

adult.relatesToToday: Parenting, grief, shift work, anxiety — the load is real. Jesus isn’t asking you to tidy up first; He asks you to come and receive rest you can’t manufacture.
adult.relatesToYou: Weariness isn’t shameful here. It’s the very reason for the invitation.
adult.realTalk: Stop trying to carry alone what was never meant to be solo. Come to Jesus; He gives rest.

catalog.quietPrayerNudge: Jesus, I come tired — give me Your rest.
verseEchoPrompts: Jesus, I come as I am — give me Your rest.
Thank You that I don’t have to carry this alone.

catalog.text: Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.

breakdown.speaker: Peter, writing to scattered believers under pressure
breakdown.audience: People carrying worry like a second job — and anyone who thinks they have to hold it all alone
breakdown.relatesToToday: In 2026 we juggle bills, kids, health, and headlines. This verse doesn’t shame the weight — it points you to hand the whole pile to God because He actually cares.
breakdown.relatesToYou: You’re allowed to offload. God isn’t annoyed by your anxiety; He invites you to cast — throw — your cares on Him.
breakdown.realTalk: Picture literally handing God a heavy bag. That’s the move. He cares for you on purpose, not as a favor you earned.

kid.relatesToToday: When worries feel huge, God says give them to Him — He cares about you.
kid.relatesToYou: You can tell Jesus what scares you. He wants to help carry it.
kid.realTalk: Hand your worries to God — He catches every one.

teen.relatesToToday: School pressure, friend drama, future noise — this verse says transfer the weight instead of white-knuckling it.
teen.relatesToYou: God cares isn’t empty talk here. It’s permission to stop pretending you’re fine.
teen.realTalk: Casting cares means honest prayer: here’s what’s eating me — I’m giving it to You.

adult.relatesToToday: Night-shift brain fog, parenting guilt, grief waves — Peter says cast, not manage perfectly.
adult.relatesToYou: His care covers the messy middle, not just the tidy prayers.
adult.realTalk: One honest unload counts. God’s shoulders are the right place for what you can’t fix tonight.

catalog.quietPrayerNudge: Lord, I cast this care on You — You care for me.
verseEchoPrompts: Lord, I cast this care on You — You care for me.
Thank You that I don’t have to carry this alone tonight.

catalog.text: Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.

breakdown.speaker: David, led by the Spirit
breakdown.audience: Anyone walking through dark valleys — grief, fear, danger, depression’s tunnel
breakdown.relatesToToday: Some days feel like a long hallway with no exit. This verse doesn’t promise the hallway disappears — it promises company: God with you, guiding, comforting.
breakdown.relatesToYou: Evil and fear don’t get the last word when you’re not walking alone. His presence is the point.
breakdown.realTalk: Valley walking is real. So is His nearness — rod and staff mean guidance and rescue, not judgment.

kid.relatesToToday: Scary times feel like a dark path. God walks right beside you.
kid.relatesToYou: You don’t have to be brave alone — God helps your heart feel safer.
kid.realTalk: In the scary part, God stays close like a good shepherd.

teen.relatesToToday: When life feels heavy or hopeless, this line says fear doesn’t have to boss you — God is with you in it.
teen.relatesToYou: The valley isn’t proof He left. It’s where shepherds stay closest.
teen.realTalk: You can tell God you’re scared and still choose to trust He’s with you.

adult.relatesToToday: Grief, trauma, chronic pain, night shifts in empty buildings — valleys look different, but the promise holds.
adult.relatesToYou: Comfort here is shepherd comfort: steady, patient, close.
adult.realTalk: You’re not melodramatic for needing this verse. Dark paths are real; His company is too.

catalog.quietPrayerNudge: Lord, walk with me in this valley — I don’t want to go alone.
verseEchoPrompts: Lord, walk with me in this valley — I don’t want to go alone.
Thank You that Your rod and staff still comfort me.

catalog.text: Have not I commanded thee? Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the LORD thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest.

breakdown.speaker: The LORD, to Joshua after Moses died
breakdown.audience: Leaders and ordinary people facing a scary next step — new territory, new responsibility
breakdown.relatesToToday: Starting over, moving cities, solo parenting, recovery — courage here isn’t swagger. It’s strength tied to God’s presence wherever you go.
breakdown.relatesToYou: Dismayed doesn’t disqualify you; it’s the very state He speaks into. He goes with you.
breakdown.realTalk: Strong and courageous doesn’t mean you’re not shaking. It means you’re not alone in the shaking.

kid.relatesToToday: New things can feel scary. God says be brave — He goes with you.
kid.relatesToYou: When you’re nervous, God is like a grown-up holding your hand in a crowd.
kid.realTalk: Brave with God means trying the hard thing — He’s there.

teen.relatesToToday: Big changes hit different. This verse ties courage to God’s presence, not to pretending you’re fearless.
teen.relatesToYou: Afraid and courageous can coexist when God is the with-you part.
teen.realTalk: Take the next step scared — His “with thee” is the fuel.

adult.relatesToToday: Court dates, hospital halls, first day alone with three kids — dismay is human; His command comes with His company.
adult.relatesToYou: You don’t manufacture courage from coffee alone. You borrow it from who walks with you.
adult.realTalk: Whithersoever is blanket coverage — night shift, funeral home, empty nursery. He’s there.

catalog.quietPrayerNudge: Lord, go with me in this next step — I’m nervous.
verseEchoPrompts: Lord, I’m stepping forward afraid — go with me.
Thank You that Your presence is my courage today.

catalog.text: Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.

breakdown.speaker: Jesus Christ, preparing His disciples for His departure
breakdown.audience: Friends about to feel abandoned and afraid — and anyone whose heart won’t settle
breakdown.relatesToToday: The world sells peace as escape, distraction, or control. Jesus gives His own peace — different source, deeper root.
breakdown.relatesToYou: Troubled hearts get addressed directly: His peace is a gift, not a prize for having it together.
breakdown.realTalk: Let not doesn’t mean flip a switch. It means His peace is real enough to lean on when your chest is tight.

kid.relatesToToday: When your heart feels jumpy, Jesus gives a special kind of quiet inside.
kid.relatesToYou: Jesus’ peace is stronger than scary thoughts — you can ask Him for it.
kid.realTalk: Jesus’ peace is like a soft blanket inside — real help, not fake happy.

teen.relatesToToday: Noise is loud online and at school. This peace isn’t the world’s cheap version.
teen.relatesToYou: You can name fear out loud and still receive what He gives.
teen.realTalk: Gift peace means you don’t earn it — you take it from His hand.

adult.relatesToToday: 2 AM spirals, marriage tension, money fear — trouble and afraid are named; so is His answer.
adult.relatesToYou: Your heart isn’t too messy for this promise.
adult.realTalk: World peace is mood. His peace holds when the circumstance doesn’t.

catalog.quietPrayerNudge: Jesus, quiet my heart with Your peace.
verseEchoPrompts: Jesus, give me Your peace — not the world’s fake calm.
Quiet my heart with what only You can give.

catalog.text: The LORD is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart; and saveth such as be of a contrite spirit.

breakdown.speaker: David, teaching God’s people to bless the Lord at all times
breakdown.audience: The crushed — brokenhearted, humbled, people who feel too messy to approach God
breakdown.relatesToToday: Grief, betrayal, diagnosis, loneliness — broken heart isn’t hidden from God; it’s where He draws near.
breakdown.relatesToYou: You don’t have to glue your heart together before you come. Near is His move toward you.
breakdown.realTalk: Contrite just means honest about the ache. That’s the exact person He saves — not the polished story.

kid.relatesToToday: When your heart feels broken, God comes close — not far away.
kid.relatesToYou: Crying doesn’t scare God off. He stays near sad kids too.
kid.realTalk: God stays near broken hearts — like a hug when words fail.

teen.relatesToToday: Heartbreak hits hard at any age. This verse says God isn’t waiting for you to “get over it.”
teen.relatesToYou: Honest sadness is a door He walks through, not a wall He avoids.

adult.relatesToToday: Miscarriage, divorce, death, estrangement — broken is descriptive, not disqualifying.
adult.relatesToYou: Salvation here includes rescue in the ache, not only after the ache ends.
adult.realTalk: You’re not too far gone if you’re honest. That’s who He saves.

catalog.quietPrayerNudge: Lord, my heart hurts — please come near.
verseEchoPrompts: Lord, my heart is broken — come near.
Thank You for saving me in my honest ache, not after I fake fine.

catalog.text: Cast thy burden upon the LORD, and he shall sustain thee: he shall never suffer the righteous to be moved.

breakdown.speaker: David, in turmoil yet preaching wisdom to his own soul
breakdown.audience: Anyone overloaded — betrayed, overwhelmed, carrying what they didn’t choose
breakdown.relatesToToday: Burdens stack: caregiving, injustice, bills, burnout. Cast isn’t poetic fluff — it’s transfer the weight and let God sustain what you cannot.
breakdown.relatesToYou: Sustain means held up when legs shake. Moved means you won’t be knocked off His care.
breakdown.realTalk: You were never meant to solo-carry infinite weight. Hand it up; He holds you up.

kid.relatesToToday: When stuff feels too heavy for your size, God says give it to Him.
kid.relatesToYou: God helps hold you up when life feels too big.
kid.realTalk: Give God your heavy load — He won’t drop you.

teen.relatesToToday: Pressure to fix everything yourself is a lie. This verse licenses transfer, not toughness theater.
teen.relatesToYou: Sustain beats swagger. Let Him hold you upright.
teen.realTalk: Cast the burden — name it, give it — then breathe.

adult.relatesToToday: Parenting alone, night shifts, legal fights — burdens have names. God sustains real people, not ideals.
adult.relatesToYou: Righteous here isn’t perfection; it’s His-side-of-the-covenant people leaning on Him.
adult.realTalk: Moved means you won’t slide off His help when you’re honest about the load.

catalog.quietPrayerNudge: Lord, this burden is Yours — sustain me today.
verseEchoPrompts: Lord, this burden is Yours — sustain me today.
I cast what I cannot carry; hold me upright.
